Andrea-lyz/ColorOS-Assistant-Restore.description: Restore AOSP digital assistant gesture behavior on the ColorOS China edition
Andrea-lyz/ColorOS-Assistant-Restore.body:
# ColorOS 唤语 · AssistRestore

Restores AOSP digital assistant behavior on the ColorOS China edition.

The domestic firmware rewrites the three entry points for "wake the digital assistant" to point to its own Xiaobu Assistant (小布助手), and makes these paths bypass AOSP's assistant dispatch. Long-pressing the power key always launches Xiaobu, long-pressing the gesture bar always triggers Xiaobu screen recognition (小布识屏), and swiping inward from a bottom corner of the screen dispatches no assistant at all. This module does not replace the system's assistant stack. It only hands the request back, at those rewritten dispatch points, to the default assistant app currently set in system settings (the app that `Settings.Secure.assistant` / `RoleManager.ROLE_ASSISTANT` points to), so that upper layers keep the same behavior as AOSP.

## Features

The three entry points use the same code on domestic and international firmware. The only differences are two regional gates and a few hardcoded component names, so each of the three paths can be taken over individually.

| Entry | Original behavior on domestic firmware | Behavior after takeover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Long-press power key | Explicitly launches `com.heytap.speechassist` | Follows the AOSP branch through `launchAssistAction` to wake the default assistant (with one long-press vibration) |
| Long-press gesture bar | `start_type=91` is handed to Xiaobu screen recognition | Wakes the default assistant; optionally switches to Circle to Search or Xiaobu screen recognition |
| Inward swipe from bottom corner | Assistant availability is always `false`, so the gesture does nothing | Restores the assistant availability check, so pages such as Settings also work |

Each entry can be given its own wake target, or turned off individually. In addition:

- **Circle to Search**: Fills in the system CTS service chain that the domestic firmware is missing for the long-press gesture bar, and can spoof the device model inside the Google app process.
- **Page-level gestures**: By default the launcher blocks the bottom-corner gesture for page requests such as Settings. The module lifts these two page-level block flags.
- **Suppressing useless wake-ups**: Long-pressing the gesture bar no longer wakes the Xiaobu screen recognition service once in advance for nothing.
- **Long-press on the gesture bar triggers only the assistant**: The gesture bar's own area (about 480×88px) belongs to the system navigation bar window, so the page no longer triggers its own long-press at the same time. The same holds when the gesture bar is hidden. When the input method is shown, this area is handed back to the keyboard.
- **Process keep-alive**: Freezing of the Google app by the system is a common cause of "dispatch succeeded but the screen does not respond". The module exempts this app from the OEM freezing decision.
- **Double-tap power key** (optional): Instead of launching ColorOS Wallet, opens the system quick wallet interface (system wallet role = Google Wallet) for card tapping.

## Requirements

- ColorOS China edition firmware (verified on ColorOS 16 `V16.1.0` and ColorOS 17 `V17.0.0.103` / PJZ110 / `regionmark=CN`).
- A root solution such as KernelSU or Magisk.
- A framework that supports the libxposed API 102, such as LSPosed.

ChurchTao/Daoyou.body:
# 万界道友

> The default entry point of this repository has moved to `NestJS + React SPA`. For the migration progress, see [Migration Record](https://github.com/ChurchTao/Daoyou/blob/HEAD/docs/nestjs-migration.md). The instructions here follow the existing code and no longer apply to the legacy Next.js architecture.

---

## Project Vision

**《万界道友》** aims to build an "open-source skeleton for a cultivation universe." It is not only a text-based cultivation game that can be played directly, but also a highly structured, AIGC-friendly underlying architecture. Through **high-freedom input + AIGC feedback**, combined with **rigorous numerical and combat models**, we hope creators can quickly build their own cultivation worlds on top of it.

- **Gameplay**: Players are encouraged to shape characters through text descriptions, with AI generating feedback in real time, delivering a "thousand players, thousand faces" experience.
- **System**: Keep the system stable, orthogonal, and composable, ensuring balanced values and self-consistent logic.
- **Presentation**: Adhere to "text as interface," using an ink-wash style UI adapted for mobile.

## Core Features

- 🤖 **Deep AIGC integration**: Character backstories, battle reports, adventure stories, and item descriptions are all generated by AI end to end, so every experience is unique. DeepSeek is currently used across the board.
- ⚔️ **Deep combat engine**: Timeline-based turn-by-turn combat supporting 神通 (divine powers), 法宝 (magic treasures), status effects (Buff/Debuff), Five Elements counters, damage pipelines, and other complex mechanics.
- ☯️ **Rigorous cultivation system**: Complete realms (Qi Refining through Tribulation Crossing), spiritual roots (Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth, Wind, Thunder, Ice), techniques, destiny traits, and alchemy and forging systems.
- 📱 **Ink-wash UI**: A pure text UI built on the `Ink` component library (21 components), simple, elegant, and immersive.
- 🛠️ **Developer-friendly**: Clear layered architecture (Engine/Service/API), full-stack TypeScript, easy to extend and remix.

「Wanjie」 lists 《万界道友》 servers deployed from this open-source repository and operated by different maintainers. Each realm may have different gameplay, settings, and community ecosystems. You are welcome to pick a world that interests you and explore it.

MoiraiLab/primetab.description: Interpretable pegRNA design with tabular foundation models
MoiraiLab/primetab.body:
# PrimeTab

**Cross-domain generalization + in-context learning (ICL) driven interpretable pegRNA automated design framework**
*Cross-domain, in-context-learning driven interpretable pegRNA design with tabular foundation models.*

PrimeTab represents Prime Editing design as **tabular features**, retrieves reference samples per candidate from historical experimental records, and then uses **TabPFN (tabular foundation model)** to predict editing efficiency via in-context learning and rank the candidates. Model weights are fixed; newly added experimental data only enters the context, enabling **training-free** adaptation to new cells / new datasets.

## Core pipeline
```
Target edit (editseq)
  → PE2-NGG candidate generation (model-free)        primetab.generation
  → 73 structured features → 107-dim input           primetab.features
  → Per-candidate reference sample retrieval         primetab.retrieval
  → TabPFN in-context learning prediction            primetab.backends / primetab.inference
  → Ranking within each editing request → candidate list   primetab.ranking
```

## Method advantages

**Training-free onboarding of new cells.** TabPFN weights are fixed; measured records from the target cell are fed directly into inference as context.
Onboarding a new cell line requires only a few dozen labeled data points and one inference pass, with no pretraining, fine-tuning, or hyperparameter search.

**Per-candidate retrieved context.** Each candidate gets its own 1000-row reference set: measured nearest neighbors in the target cell, plus samples retrieved from the source pool jointly by feature distribution and label. When the same model instead used a randomly drawn shared context of 8023 rows, its eight-cell macro-average Spearman was 0.648; the per-candidate retrieved 1000-row context gave 0.757.

**Stable across cells.** Achieved the highest Spearman across nine target conditions (eight cell lines plus in vivo mouse hepatocyte data), with an eight-cell macro-average of 0.757 versus 0.698 for the runner-up. On HepG2, which has the fewest labels (12 records), it scored 0.388 versus 0.316 for the runner-up.

**End-to-end traceability.** Runs from `editseq` to the candidate list in one pass, outputting the candidate table, feature table, ranking results, NGS primers, and a `manifest.json` with checksums. Perturbing a single feature yields the predicted response, linking ranking results to specific design variables.

## Installation
```bash
pip install -e ".[tfm]"        # includes TabPFN inference
pip install -e ".[tfm,baselines,dev]"
```

Feature engineering depends on ViennaRNA and Biopython; TabPFN…

Nanako0129/shanjie.body:
# shanjie (善解)

An open-source macOS Zhuyin input method that puts correct character selection first (under continuous development).

- Plan: `docs/PLAN.md`
- License: code under Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`); data see `LICENSES/data.md`
- Want to contribute: see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Nanako0129/shanjie/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Progress

For the latest release, see [Releases' Latest](https://github.com/Nanako0129/shanjie/releases/latest): a Zhuyin input method ready to install and use. Changes in each version are in the release notes (`docs/releases/`).
- Standard and Eten keyboard layouts; whole-sentence conversion (lexicon + bigram language model + part-of-speech fallback); Ministry of Education "一／不／法" pronunciation variants.
- Character selection using preceding text: reads the characters already committed before the cursor, then uses them to select the first word of this segment.
- Real-time prediction: type the first Zhuyin symbol of the next word, and the candidate window lists words that fit the preceding text (Tab enters selection; the menu can turn it off).
- Selection memory: learns from changing candidates in the candidate window and from selections in the prediction bar, stored separately per preceding text; single characters are applied only when the preceding text is exactly the same; a confirmation dialog appears before clearing.
- A custom Liquid Glass candidate bar that follows the app's light and dark appearance; punctuation shows the same names as Apple's; pressing ↓ stacks more candidate bars downward, with 9 candidates per bar.
- `[`、`]`、`\`、`` ` `` type punctuation without Shift, and so do `'` and `=` on the standard keyboard (matching Apple Zhuyin; on the Eten keyboard these two keys are Zhuyin); when the composition area is empty, pressing a tone key types the tone mark.

**v0.4.0 released** (2026-10-10, notes at `docs/releases/v0.4.0.md`): a new installer, updates no longer break Caps Lock switching, a settings window, vertical candidate window, anime and game word packs (about 30,000 work and character names, can be turned off in the menu), a new language model model-v5, Enter sends unfinished Zhuyin, and the predictive start point looks back 5 syllables. The word pack source is Chinese Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0).

**Next version**: v0.4.1, fixing user-reported issues (candidate window position in browsers, name entries containing interpunct, missing names and readings); see the v0.4.1 section of `docs/PLAN.md`. App sandboxing is scheduled for v0.5.0. Omittable finals are implemented but hidden for now (whole-sentence abbreviation is not done yet); new words and other characters not moving after a reselection come later.

See `docs/PLAN.md` §2 "版本對應" (version mapping) for details.

| Stage | Content | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Lexicon and candidates (S1, L) | Openly licensed lexicon, compact format, candidate generation | Done |
| Language model (S2) | bigram whole-sentence conversion, pronunciation variants, preceding-text selection, part-of-speech fallback | Along…

# furigana-dict

> Japanese word dictionary for the [furigana](https://github.com/RyuuNeko1107/ja-furigana) library — open, community-maintained.

A standalone repository that hosts the **vocabulary dictionary** used by [`furigana`](https://github.com/RyuuNeko1107/ja-furigana) (furigana API + library). Adding or correcting readings is done entirely by **editing TOML and submitting a PR**.

> For the latest counts / per-category breakdown / sizes, see [**STATS.md**](https://github.com/RyuuNeko1107/ja-furigana-dict/blob/HEAD/STATS.md)
> (GitHub Actions auto-commits on master push; contributors don't need to do anything).
> For the latest release, see [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/RyuuNeko1107/ja-furigana-dict/releases).

> 🔍 **Search, filter, and browse all entries on the web**:
> <https://ryuuneko1107.github.io/ja-furigana-dict/>
> ([`tools/build_dict_browser.py`](https://github.com/RyuuNeko1107/ja-furigana-dict/blob/HEAD/tools/build_dict_browser.py) is auto-deployed on every master push via
> [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/RyuuNeko1107/ja-furigana-dict/blob/HEAD/.github/workflows/build-pages.yml). Features include per-kanji sweep progress management, detection of redundant jukugo, and a `[[kanji]]` block detail view.)

## Why a separate repository?

As the number of dictionary entries grew, managing them alongside the main library's code repository became cumbersome, so they were split out.
The dictionary is fetched via `furigana dict pull`, which downloads a tar.gz from GitHub Release.

## Structure

```
core/
├── jukugo/<genre>/   ← jukugo (compound words) and proper nouns (basic / humanities /…
```

guesung/Web-Memo.body:
---

## 🤔 Background of Development

Hello! Web Memo is a project that grew out of the inconvenience I felt while reading web pages. I'm sure you've had similar experiences.

### 1. The hassle of taking notes

While reading an article, there are times when you think, "I should keep a record of this." Each time, I had to open a notes app and split the screen in half to write things down, which was tedious. This experience made me feel that I needed a way to record everything at once without opening a separate notes app.

### 2. The hassle of writing the title and URL every time

After opening a notes app, I had to manually enter the title and URL to record which article the note came from. I started wondering whether there was a way to handle this automatically.

### ⇒ "Web Memo"

Based on these experiences, I developed an extension that lets you **take notes easily while reading articles**! Web Memo was created to relieve the inconvenience I experienced and to help others take notes more easily.

Web Memo will make your article reading time more relaxed. With Web Memo, you can build a systematic note-taking system so you don't miss important information while reading and can easily find it later.

Enjoy a richer web browsing experience with Web Memo!

---

# All-Japan-Grid

See, check, and use the national transmission grid of Japan, with sources.
A national transmission grid model assembled automatically from OpenStreetMap and cross-checked against utilities' published materials.
Beyond viewing it on a map, you can solve power flow, draw inside substations, and test what happens during disasters.
Every assumption made in the model and where it was applied can be traced in the registry.

**See, check and use Japan's transmission grid — with sources.** An open model of the national grid,
built automatically from OpenStreetMap and checked against what the utilities publish. It renders on a
map, solves power flow, draws every substation, and lets you stress-test it — and every modelling
assumption is listed in a registry you can read.

scottfly189/WeChatAuto.SDK.body:
# WECHATAUTO.SDK - A Modern AI-Oriented WeChat RPA Automation Framework

WeChatAuto.SDK is an AI-oriented WeChat RPA automation SDK built on .NET and UI automation technology. It is designed for scenarios that integrate artificial intelligence, such as LLM context interaction. The SDK provides a rich, intuitive API, supports modern .NET features such as dependency injection, and also offers an official Python SDK, so you can easily integrate WeChat automation workflows into existing systems.

## ✨ Features

- 💬 **Comprehensive messaging and social capabilities** - Supports sending text, emoji, files, @mentions, message forwarding, group management, Moments operations, and contact management, and provides common capabilities such as message listening; all important interfaces are covered by unit tests.
  
- 🛡️ **Lower anti-abuse risk** - Supports pure software automation as well as solutions combined with hardware keyboard and mouse simulators, so you can choose a more robust execution method based on business needs and security level.

- 🚀 **Multi-instance and distributed support** - Can manage multiple WeChat clients at the same time. It can be used as a local SDK, or through a WebSocket long connection, allowing one application to control multiple WeChat instances on multiple machines, or multiple applications to control the same WeChat instance.

- 🔧 **WeChat version compatibility** - Compatible with older (e.g., 3.9.12.xx) and newer (e.g., 4.1.11.xx) WeChat versions, and continuously updated to adapt to new client releases.

- 🧩 **Multi-language support** - Natively developed in .NET, and also provides an official Python SDK for integration across different language ecosystems.

- 🔌 **Easy integration and high reliability** - Supports dependency injection and is a lightweight SDK that is easy to embed in existing systems. Uses industrial-grade thread management and stability design to reduce the risk of UI automation freezing.

- 🤖 **AI-friendly** - Natively supports LLM context integration and includes a built-in MCP Server, making it easy to connect with mainstream agents and platforms and helping intelligent applications close the loop on WeChat automation / RPA and extend it.

> 👉 If you find this helpful, please like, Star, and Fork this project so you don't lose track of it. Thanks for your support!

> 👉 If you'd like to try WeChatAuto.SDK's capabilities, I have set up a test navigation bot. Feel free to add it on WeChat to try it out. 👉 [Try it here](https://github.com/scottfly189/WeChatAuto.SDK/blob/HEAD/MD/Experience.md)

## 🎉 Important Notice!!

**WeChatAuto.SDK** provides two versions of the SDK:
